analyst_view.overall: Kairat (27th of 36, two points from three games) host Mjällby (9th, seven points) in Almaty on matchday 4, needing a win to climb out of the elimination places after a 1-1 draw at Atalanta. Kairat's domestic season ended about two weeks before this match, they are run by interim coach Zhora Harutyunyan with no permanent manager, and a former Kairat defender told local media the squad is short of match sharpness and in a poor frame of mind; their poor recent shooting and leaky defence (14 conceded in six) are already in the numbers. Mjällby are still in season and fresher, mid-table in the Allsvenskan with one league round left, but forward Jacob Bergström went off with a thigh strain in the 1-1 draw with Malmö on 21 November and is a doubt; Dalsgaard and Stavitski (in the numbers) are out. Specific team news for Kairat was thin and no referee is named yet, so the view rests mainly on the rest-versus-rhythm contrast and will be refreshed nearer kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals, already trimming Kairat for scoring only 3 in their last six. Kairat's long break could blunt their attack but also loosen a defence that shipped five at home to Panathinaikos, and Bergström's doubt for Mjällby points slightly down, so with these pulling both ways I stay at 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, already cutting Kairat for winning just 12 in their last six. Mjällby, as the fresher side still in season, may have more of the ball than usual for an away team, which the near-even split (4.4 to 4.3) already reflects, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, with Mjällby's quiet disciplinary record taking a little off. No referee has been named yet and neither side has a rivalry or bad-tempered history here; a Kairat side under pressure to win at home could commit more fouls, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 4.5 until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots and already take about 7% off Kairat for their low recent shooting. I trim a little more, to about 24.2, because Kairat come in with no competitive game for around three weeks and no permanent coach, and Mjällby may be without Bergström, one of their forwards; the numbers can't see either.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already cutting Kairat by about 10% for only 14 on target in six and lifting Mjällby for their accurate recent shooting. Kairat's lack of match rhythm since their league season ended and Bergström's doubt point a little lower, so I go to about 8.1.
